The manuscript and its formalization have different jobs. The LaTeX source supplies the mathematical exposition. Agda supplies explicit types and derivations against the stated interface.

Reading code beside the book

  1. Click dotted-underlined prose to open the right-hand Agda reader. For example, “There are categories” highlights CAT : Set c. Code is hidden initially.
  2. All associated lines in the module stand out together, for example isAn and the fields of AN for animae. The reader moves to the first highlighted line. All code is fully visible and scrolls independently. The Module menu opens any available module, grouped into related and other checked files.
  3. Click a line number or unlinked code text to highlight that line and move the book to its corresponding passage. More specific proof steps take precedence over enclosing declarations. A Book passage menu appears when there are alternatives. Unassigned lines leave the book in place.
  4. Some links work only from code to prose: Iso₃ returns to “The same construction may be iterated.” That explanatory sentence remains unclickable.
  5. Copy selection copies exactly the highlighted lines. Follow Full module, or Ctrl/Command-click a symbol, to inspect its definition and dependencies. Close with × or Escape. Keyboard activation enters the controls; Escape returns to the selected prose. Narrow screens use a bottom tray.

The source is highlighted and linked by Agda itself. Snippets are extracted from that output and verified against the source snapshot. This is inspection of checked code; typechecking runs during the build.

Following definitions

Click a linked Agda identifier to jump to its definition inside the code reader, including definitions in imported modules and local bindings. The book stays in place. Back in code returns to the previous highlights and scroll position. Click a line number or unlinked code text to navigate back to prose. Ctrl/Command-click opens the usual full-module link.

What the statuses mean

  1. Assumption, boundary checked: a field of an input record. Agda checks that its type is well formed. It does not derive that field.
  2. Derived, checked against supplied interface: a proof using the module parameters and imports.
  3. Definition, checked: a checked construction whose type is displayed.

These checks do not construct a model or prove consistency. The underlined headings retain the manuscript's intended validity in categorical contexts. That marking and its later justification are separate from the absolute Agda development.

Notation at a glance

AgdaReading
CAT, MAP C DCategories and functors.
ObjAbs CAn absolute object, a functor from the terminal anima.
NatIso f gA natural isomorphism.
Iso₂ α βAn identification between natural isomorphisms.
_∙_, _◁_, _▷_, _⋆_Vertical composition, postwhiskering, prewhiskering, horizontal composition.
{A : CAT}An implicit parameter category. Its occurrence in a signature remains visible.

All the code

The all-code index contains every source module in the web edition, with a searchable declaration index for checked modules. Full module pages offer a generated list of corresponding book passages.

How the files should grow

Keep the present chapter and section modules, with Everything.agda aggregates for checking. Give each theorem a readable public entry point; keep long supporting calculations in imported modules. Let the correspondence manifest arrange the reading order independently of the dependency order.

Prefer actual family theorems as entry points, with their absolute specializations and comparison bridges linked explicitly. A future readability refactor can name typed intermediate steps in composition proofs. This web edition reads the annotated manuscript and the Agda sources maintained for publication, with isAn moved before MAP to match the opening prose. AN stays in its original position. Record definitions highlight their fields; selected local proof steps highlight their bindings or arguments in the surrounding module.

Maintainers can read the comparison of three integration options.

Reading preferences

Select Hide links to Agda code for plain book text without Agda underlines, tooltips, or standalone code badges. The preference is remembered across pages. Browse Agda modules opens the reader independently of prose links. The module browser contains the checked dependency closure for the selected sections.
